questions.question: The Union Public Service Commission submits its annual report to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** is mandated by **Article 323(1)** of the **Constitution of India** to submit an annual report directly to the **President** of India, detailing the work performed by the Commission over the preceding year.
 
• The **President** is then constitutionally obligated to place this report before both Houses of **Parliament** (the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**), ensuring that the activities of the Commission are scrutinized by the legislative branch.
 
• Accompanying the report is a **memorandum** that must explain the reasons why the advice of the Commission was not accepted by the government in any specific instances, which serves as a safeguard against arbitrary executive decisions in civil service matters.
 
• Established under **Articles 315 to 323** in **Part XIV** of the Constitution, the **UPSC** acts as an independent constitutional body to maintain the merit system of the **Indian Civil Services** without political interference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Public Service Commission (SPSC)**:

 
 
• According to **Article 323(2)**, the **SPSC** follows a similar protocol at the state level by submitting its annual report to the **Governor** of the state, who then places it before the **State Legislature**.
 
 
 
• **Appointment and Removal**:
 
 
• The **Chairman** and members of the **UPSC** are appointed by the **President** for a term of six years or until they reach the age of **65 years**.
 
• They can be removed by the **President** only on the grounds of misbehavior after an inquiry by the **Supreme Court**, as per **Article 317**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Other Entities**:
 
 
• **Parliament**: While **Parliament** discusses the report, it is the **President** who facilitates the submission process.
 
• **Prime Minister**: As the head of the **Union Council of Ministers**, the **Prime Minister** oversees the executive branch, but the **UPSC** remains an autonomous body reporting to the **Head of State** to preserve its neutrality.
 
• **Cabinet Secretary**: The highest-ranking civil servant who heads the **Cabinet Secretariat**, yet the **UPSC** operates outside this administrative hierarchy for recruitment and disciplinary functions.

questions.question: A bill passed by both houses becomes law after:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President's assent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 111** of the **Constitution of India**, when a **Bill** has been passed by both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**, it must be presented to the **President** for their formal approval.
 
• The legislative process is completed only when the **President** provides their **assent**, at which stage the **Bill** officially becomes an **Act** or a law of the land.
 
• The **President** holds the authority to exercise **Veto Powers**; they can either grant **assent**, withhold **assent**, or return the **Bill** (except for a **Money Bill**) for reconsideration by the **Parliament**.
 
• If the **Parliament** passes the **Bill** again, with or without changes, and presents it to the **President** a second time, the **President** is constitutionally bound to give their **assent**.
 
• Once **assent** is received, the law is typically published in the **Official Gazette of India** to inform the public of its commencement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**:

 
 
• The **Supreme Court** does not approve bills; instead, it exercises **Judicial Review** under **Article 13** to ensure that the laws enacted do not violate the **Fundamental Rights** or the **Basic Structure** of the **Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendment Bills**:
 
 
• Under **Article 368**, the **President** has no power to return or withhold **assent** for a **Constitutional Amendment Bill**; they must sign it once it is passed by the required majority in both houses.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Components**:
 
 
• As per **Article 79**, the **Parliament of India** consists of the **President**, the **Council of States (Rajya Sabha)**, and the **House of the People (Lok Sabha)**. Therefore, the **President** is an integral part of the legislative body.
 
 
 
• **Money Bills**:
 
 
• A **Money Bill**, defined under **Article 110**, is introduced only in the **Lok Sabha** with the prior recommendation of the **President**, and the **President** generally grants **assent** to it.

questions.question: During which festival is the Bihu dance primarily performed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bihu dance** is an indigenous folk dance from the Indian state of **Assam**, performed primarily during the **Bihu festival**, which marks the most important cultural celebration of the Assamese people.
 
• While there are three types of Bihu, the dance is most vigorously performed during **Rongali Bihu** (also known as **Bohag Bihu**), which occurs in **mid-April** to celebrate the **Assamese New Year** and the onset of the **spring season**.
 
• The performance is characterized by **brisk dance steps**, **rapid hand movements**, and a rhythmic swaying of the hips, symbolizing **fertility**, **youth**, and the **joy of nature**.
 
• Dancers wear traditional Assamese attire; women wear the **Mekhela Chador** made of **Muga silk** (golden silk), and men wear **Dhoti** and **Gamosa**.
 
• The musical accompaniment includes traditional instruments such as the **Dhol** (a two-sided drum), **Pepa** (an instrument made of buffalo horn), **Gogona** (a reed/bamboo instrument), **Toka** (a bamboo clapper), and **Xutuli** (a clay whistle).
 
• In **April 2023**, the Bihu dance created a **Guinness World Record** when over **11,000 dancers and drummers** performed together at the **Sarusajai Stadium** in **Guwahati**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diwali**:

 
 
• Known as the **Festival of Lights**, it is celebrated across **India** to signify the victory of light over darkness and good over evil.
 
• It usually falls between **mid-October and mid-November** and involves the lighting of **Diyas** and **fireworks**.
 
 
 
• **Durga Puja**:
 
 
• A major festival celebrated with great fervor in **West Bengal**, **Odisha**, and **Assam**, honoring the victory of **Goddess Durga** over the demon **Mahishasura**.
 
• It is inscribed on the **UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.
 
 
 
• **Pongal**:
 
 
• A four-day **harvest festival** celebrated in **Tamil Nadu** and by the Tamil diaspora worldwide, dedicated to the **Sun God** (Surya).
 
• It typically occurs in **January** and coincides with **Makar Sankranti**, marking the start of the sun's six-month-long journey northwards (**Uttarayanam**).

questions.question: Which place is the most famous center for Hola Mohalla celebrations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anandpur Sahib**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hola Mohalla** is a prominent **Sikh festival** that takes place annually at **Anandpur Sahib** in the state of **Punjab**, attracting millions of devotees from across the globe.
 
• The festival was started by the tenth Sikh Guru, **Guru Gobind Singh Ji**, in **March 1701**, originally designed as a day for the **Khalsa** to perform military exercises and mock battles.
 
• The term **Hola** is a masculine variation of the word Holi, while **Mohalla** signifies an **organized procession** or a military-style column.
 
• The celebrations span three days and include a massive display of **martial arts**, such as **Gatka** (traditional weapon-based fighting), **tent pegging**, and bareback **horse riding**.
 
• The event serves as a platform for **poetry competitions** and **kirtan** (spiritual music), reinforcing the Sikh values of **chardi kala** (eternal optimism) and **valour**.
 
• The festivities culminate in a grand procession led by the **Panj Pyaras**, starting from **Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib** and passing through various historical **Gurdwaras**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anandpur Sahib**:

 
 
• Founded in **1665** by **Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji**, the ninth Sikh Guru, it is known as the **City of Bliss**.
 
• It is the historical site where the **Khalsa Panth** was formally established during the **Vaisakhi** of **1699**.
 
• The city houses **Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib**, which is one of the five **Takhts** (seats of authority) of Sikhism.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Sikh Centers**:
 
 
• **Amritsar**: Established by **Guru Ram Das Ji**, it is the site of the **Harmandir Sahib** (Golden Temple) and serves as the spiritual hub of the community.
 
• **Patna Sahib**: Located in **Bihar**, this is the **birthplace** of **Guru Gobind Singh Ji** and is recognized as a **Takht**.
 
• **Nankana Sahib**: Currently located in **Pakistan**, it is the sacred birthplace of **Guru Nanak Dev Ji**, the founder of Sikhism.

questions.question: The weight of an object on the moon is approximately what fraction of its weight on Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1/6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **weight** of an object is defined as the **gravitational force** exerted on it by a celestial body. It is mathematically expressed as the product of the object's **mass** (m) and the **acceleration due to gravity** (g) of that body.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity** on the surface of the **Moon** is approximately **1.625 m/s²**, whereas the standard gravity on **Earth** is approximately **9.807 m/s²**.
 
• By comparing these two values, the ratio of the **lunar gravity** to **terrestrial gravity** is calculated as 1.625 ÷ 9.807, which is approximately **0.1657**, or nearly **1/6**.
 
• The Moon's gravity is significantly lower because its **mass** is about **1/81** of the Earth's mass and its **radius** is only **1/3.7** of the Earth's radius.
 
• Consequently, an object with a weight of **600 Newtons** on Earth would weigh approximately **100 Newtons** on the Moon, although its **mass remains constant** in both environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Differences**:

 
 
• **Mass**: Measured in **kilograms (kg)**, mass is the measure of the quantity of matter in an object. It is a **scalar quantity** and is **invariant** across the universe.
 
• **Weight**: Measured in **Newtons (N)**, weight is a **vector quantity** that changes depending on the strength of the local **gravitational field**.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Formula**:
 
 
• The value of **g** is determined by **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**: **g = G × M / R²**, where **G** is the **Universal Gravitational Constant** (6.674 × 10−¹¹ Nm²/kg²), **M** is the **mass** of the celestial body, and **R** is its **radius**.
 
• This **inverse-square law** indicates that while a smaller radius increases gravity, the Moon's significantly lower mass is the dominant factor in making its gravity **one-sixth** that of Earth.

questions.question: Who is the author of To Kill a Mockingbird?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harper Lee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harper Lee**, born Nelle Harper Lee in **1926**, was an iconic **American novelist** whose reputation rests primarily on her debut novel, **'To Kill a Mockingbird'**, published in **1960**.
 
• The novel was an immediate success, winning the prestigious **Pulitzer Prize for Fiction** in **1961** and becoming a staple of **modern American literature** taught in schools worldwide.
 
• The story is set in the fictional town of **Maycomb, Alabama**, during the **Great Depression** and is narrated by **Jean Louise 'Scout' Finch**, a young girl learning about social injustice and moral fortitude.
 
• The narrative centers on **Atticus Finch**, a principled lawyer who defends **Tom Robinson**, a Black man falsely accused of raping a white woman, highlighting themes of **racial prejudice** and the loss of innocence.
 
• Lee was awarded the **Presidential Medal of Freedom** in **2007** for her contribution to literature, and her second novel, **'Go Set a Watchman'**, was published much later in **2015** as an earlier draft of her masterpiece.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Margaret Atwood**:

 
 
• A prolific **Canadian author** known for her **speculative fiction** and environmental activism.
 
• Her most famous work is **'The Handmaid's Tale'** (1985), which explores a **dystopian society** centered on **theocratic totalitarianism**.
 
 
 
• **Toni Morrison**:
 
 
• A Nobel Prize-winning **American novelist** celebrated for her examination of the **Black female experience**.
 
• Major works include **'Beloved'** (1987), which won the **Pulitzer Prize**, and **'The Bluest Eye'** (1970).
 
 
 
• **Sylvia Plath**:
 
 
• A renowned **American poet** and novelist associated with the **Confessional poetry** movement.
 
• She is best known for her semi-autobiographical novel **'The Bell Jar'** (1963) and the posthumous poetry collection **'Ariel'**.

questions.question: Which survey data is mainly used to calculate the Happiness Index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gallup World Poll**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Happiness Report** is an annual publication of the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network** (SDSN) that ranks global happiness levels based on survey data.
 
• The primary source of data used for the index is the **Gallup World Poll**, which conducts surveys in more than **160 countries** and in over **140 languages** to capture the perspectives of respondents worldwide.
 
• The core measure used is the **Cantril Self-Anchoring Striving Scale** (or Cantril Ladder), where participants rate their current life on a scale from **0 to 10**, where 10 represents the best possible life.
 
• The index analyzes six key factors to explain the variation in happiness: **GDP per capita**, **social support**, **healthy life expectancy**, **freedom to make life choices**, **generosity**, and **perceptions of corruption**.
 
• The first **World Happiness Report** was released in **April 2012**, following the **UN High-Level Meeting** on 'Happiness and Well-Being: Defining a New Economic Paradigm'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pew Global Attitudes Survey**

 
 
• A series of worldwide public opinion surveys conducted by the **Pew Research Center**.
 
• It focuses on subjects ranging from people's assessment of their own lives to their views on the **global economy**, **technology**, and **international policy**.
 
 
 
• **Transparency International Survey**
 
 
• This organization is best known for the **Corruption Perceptions Index** (CPI).
 
• The survey measures the perceived levels of **public sector corruption** in countries around the world based on expert assessments and opinion surveys.
 
 
 
• **World Bank Enterprise Survey**
 
 
• A firm-level survey that collects data from a representative sample of an economy's **private sector**.
 
• It covers topics such as **access to finance**, **corruption**, **infrastructure**, **crime**, and **performance indicators** like sales and employment growth.

questions.question: Which layer of the Sun is visible during a total solar eclipse?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Corona**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Corona** is the outermost layer of the **solar atmosphere**, extending millions of kilometers into space and consisting of extremely hot, low-density **plasma**.
 
• Under ordinary conditions, the **Corona** is invisible to the human eye because its light is approximately **one million times fainter** than that of the **Photosphere**.
 
• During a **total solar eclipse**, the **Moon** moves directly between the **Earth** and the **Sun**, completely occulting the bright **solar disk** and revealing the **Corona** as a shimmering, pearly white **halo**.
 
• Scientifically, the **Corona** is noted for its extreme temperatures, which range from **1 million** to **3 million degrees Celsius**, far exceeding the surface temperature of the **Sun**.
 
• The structure and appearance of the **Corona** are dictated by the **Sun magnetic field**, often appearing as streamers, loops, or plumes that fluctuate with the **11-year solar cycle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosphere**:

 
 
• It is the **visible surface** of the **Sun** that we see daily, with a thickness of about **500 kilometers**.
 
• This layer has a temperature of roughly **5,500 degrees Celsius** and is where **sunspots** are formed.
 
 
 
• **Chromosphere**:
 
 
• Located above the **Photosphere**, this layer is approximately **2,000 kilometers** thick.
 
• It emits a distinctive **reddish glow** due to **hydrogen** heating, which is briefly visible at the beginning and end of a **total solar eclipse** as the **flash spectrum**.
 
 
 
• **Core**:
 
 
• The **innermost region** where **nuclear fusion** occurs, converting **hydrogen** into **helium** at temperatures reaching **15 million degrees Celsius**.
 
• The **Core** is never visible from **Earth** as it is contained within the dense **solar interior**.

questions.question: Which country, other than Central Asian nations, directly benefits from Chabahar Port through India's aid delivery?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Afghanistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chabahar Port** is a strategic maritime facility located on the **Makran Coast** in the **Sistan and Baluchestan Province** of **Iran**, situated along the **Gulf of Oman**.
 
• It serves as a vital transit hub that allows **India** to bypass **Pakistan** to access landlocked **Afghanistan** and the **Central Asian Republics** (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan).
 
• In **May 2016**, **India**, **Iran**, and **Afghanistan** signed a trilateral **Chabahar Agreement** to establish a transport and transit corridor, facilitating the movement of goods and services between the three nations.
 
• India has actively utilized the port to deliver humanitarian assistance to **Afghanistan**, including the shipment of **75,000 metric tonnes of wheat** as food aid and **20,000 litres of Malathion** to help the country combat locust infestations.
 
• The port development is led by **India Ports Global Limited (IPGL)**, which operates the **Shahid Beheshti** terminal, ensuring a steady supply chain for essential commodities to the Afghan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strategic Connectivity**:

 
 
• **Zaranj-Delaram Road**: India constructed this **218-km** highway in **Afghanistan** to connect the **Iran-Afghanistan border** to the **Garland Highway**, linking major Afghan cities like Kabul, Kandahar, and Herat to the Chabahar Port.
 
• **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**: Chabahar is envisioned as a key gateway for this **7,200-km** multi-modal network designed to connect **India**, **Iran**, **Azerbaijan**, and **Russia**.
 
• **Geopolitical Context**: The port is strategically positioned to compete with **Pakistan's Gwadar Port**, which is being developed with significant **Chinese** investment under the **CPEC** framework.
 
 
 
• **Regional Impact**:
 
 
• **Pakistan**: Does not benefit from this initiative as it provides an alternative that reduces **Afghanistan's** dependence on Pakistani ports like Karachi.
 
• **Myanmar and Sri Lanka**: These nations are geographically distant and rely on **Bay of Bengal** and **Indian Ocean** maritime routes, bearing no direct connection to the transit logic of **Chabahar**.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly links a Five-Year Plan with the main challenge it faced?

options.text: First Plan - inflationary pressures from industrialization
Third Plan – food crisis and Indo-China war
Fourth Plan - heavy industrial investment shortages
Fifth Plan – underutilization of foreign exchange reserves

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Plan - food crisis and Indo-China war**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** (1951–1956) was based on the **Harrod-Domar model** and primarily focused on the **agricultural sector**, irrigation, and power to overcome food shortages; it was largely successful and did not suffer from industrial inflationary pressures. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan** (1961–1966) aimed for a **self-reliant** and **self-generating economy** but was severely hampered by the **Sino-Indian War** of **1962** and the **Indo-Pakistani War** of **1965**, which diverted funds to **defense spending**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• In addition to war, the **Third Plan** period witnessed a disastrous **drought** in **1965-66**, leading to a critical **food crisis** and necessitating massive imports under the **PL-480 program**, which eventually led to the **Plan Holidays** (1966–1969). ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan** (1969–1974) focused on **Growth with Stability** and the **progressive achievement of self-reliance**, but its main challenges were the **1971 Bangladesh refugee crisis** and the global **1973 oil shock**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Fifth Five-Year Plan** (1974–1978) focused on **Garibi Hatao** (Poverty Eradication) and **attainment of self-reliance**; it did not face a primary challenge regarding the underutilization of **foreign exchange reserves**, which actually grew during later periods. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission of India**:

 
 
• Established in **March 1950** as a non-constitutional and advisory body to formulate India's Five-Year Plans.
 
• The **Prime Minister** served as the **Ex-officio Chairman**, while the **Deputy Chairman** handled the administrative transition of the plans.
 
• Replaced by **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) on **January 1, 2015**, to foster **cooperative federalism**.
 
 
 
• **Important Plan Outcomes**:
 
 
• **Second Plan (1956-61)**: Known as the **Mahalanobis Plan**, it focused on **rapid industrialization** and **heavy industries**.
 
• **Plan Holiday (1966-69)**: Three annual plans were implemented due to the economic exhaustion following the **Third Plan's** failure.
 
• **Rolling Plan (1978-80)**: Introduced by the **Janata Party government** after terminating the **Fifth Plan** one year early.

questions.question: The Life Insurance Corporation of India was established in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1956**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)** was established on **September 1, 1956**, after the Government of India decided to nationalize the private insurance industry.
 
• The legislative framework for this transition was the **Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956**, which was passed by the Parliament on **June 19, 1956**.
 
• The formation of LIC involved the merger of over **245 insurance companies** and provident societies, which were previously functioning as private entities in the Indian market.
 
• The central objective behind the nationalization was to mobilize **domestic savings** for the purpose of nation-building and to provide financial security to the **rural population** of India at an affordable cost.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Attributes of LIC**:

 
 
• **Headquarters**: The central office of LIC is located in **Mumbai**, Maharashtra.
 
• **Slogan**: The corporation operates under the motto **'Yogakshemam Vahamyaham'**, which is a Sanskrit phrase meaning 'Your welfare is our responsibility', sourced from the **9th chapter of the Bhagavad Gita**.
 
• **Governance**: It is a **statutory body** under the jurisdiction of the **Ministry of Finance**, Government of India.
 
• **Market Status**: For nearly **44 years**, LIC enjoyed a complete monopoly in the life insurance sector until the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA) Act, 1999** opened the sector to private competitors in the year **2000**.
 
• **Investment Role**: LIC is currently the largest **institutional investor** in India, significantly contributing to the government's **Five-Year Plans** and various **infrastructure development** initiatives.

questions.question: Which soil is best suited for cotton cultivation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Black soil**, also known as **Regur soil** or **Black Cotton Soil**, is the most suitable soil type for **cotton cultivation** due to its unique chemical and physical properties.
 
• It is primarily found in the **Deccan Trap** region, covering states like **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, and **Madhya Pradesh**, and is formed from the weathering of **basaltic lava rocks**.
 
• The soil is characterized by a high **clay content**, which provides it with an exceptional **moisture-retention capacity**, allowing the cotton crop to thrive even during periods of low rainfall.
 
• A distinctive feature of this soil is its **self-ploughing** nature; it develops deep **fissures** or cracks during the dry season, which facilitates **oxygenation** and **aeration** of the soil layers.
 
• Chemically, **Black soil** is rich in essential nutrients such as **calcium carbonate**, **magnesium**, **potash**, and **lime**, though it is typically deficient in **phosphorus** and **nitrogen**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Red Soil**:

 
 
• Formed from **crystalline igneous rocks** in regions with low rainfall, such as parts of **Tamil Nadu** and **Odisha**.
 
• It appears red due to the high diffusion of **iron oxides** and is better suited for **pulses** and **millets**.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Soil**:
 
 
• Deposited by **Himalayan rivers**, it is the most fertile and widespread soil in **India**, particularly in the **Indo-Gangetic plains**.
 
• It is ideal for **intensive agriculture**, supporting crops like **paddy**, **wheat**, and **sugarcane**.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil**:
 
 
• Develops in areas with **high temperature** and **heavy rainfall** through the process of intense **leaching**.
 
• It is acidic and nutrient-poor but is highly effective for **plantation crops** like **cashew nuts**, **tea**, and **coffee**.

questions.question: What does the Urban Challenge Fund support?

options.text: ₹1 lakh crore for urban redevelopment, cities as growth hubs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1 lakh crore for urban redevelopment, cities as growth hubs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Urban Challenge Fund** is a strategic initiative aimed at incentivizing states to undertake significant **urban reforms** and modernize their cities.
 
• As per the **Union Budget 2024-25**, the government has proposed an allocation of **₹1 lakh crore** to support states in implementing these reforms and fostering **urban redevelopment**.
 
• The primary objective of this fund is to transform cities into **growth hubs** by improving **urban planning**, governance, and economic productivity, which are essential for achieving the vision of a **Viksit Bharat**.
 
• Support is specifically directed toward high-impact projects such as **water supply**, **sewerage systems**, and **solid waste management** across several large cities through bankable projects.
 
• The fund encourages a competitive approach among states, rewarding those that successfully implement **orderly urban growth** policies and sustainable infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cities as Growth Hubs**:

 
 
• Refers to the development of urban centers as concentrated areas of **economic activity**, innovation, and employment.
 
• Focuses on creating **social and physical infrastructure** that attracts global and domestic investment to boost the national **GDP**.
 
 
 
• **Urban Redevelopment**:
 
 
• Involves the restoration and modernization of older city areas, including **slum redevelopment** and revitalizing commercial zones.
 
• Emphasizes **Transit-Oriented Development (TOD)** and the efficient use of **urban land** to accommodate rising populations.
 
 
 
• **Urban Reforms**:
 
 
• Includes legislative and administrative changes like reforming **property tax** structures, updating **building bylaws**, and streamlining **urban planning** processes.

questions.question: The Mughal policy of Sulh-i-Kul emphasized:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Religious tolerance and universal peace**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sulh-i-Kul** is a **Persian** phrase that literally translates to 'absolute peace' or 'universal peace', serving as the foundational ideology of **Emperor Akbar's** reign during the **Mughal Empire**.
 
• This policy was formulated to unify a socially and religiously diverse **India**, moving away from orthodox sectarianism toward a state policy that treated all religious communities with equal respect.
 
• The concept was heavily influenced by **Akbar's** interactions at the **Ibadat Khana** (House of Worship) in **Fatehpur Sikri**, where he held debates with scholars from **Hinduism**, **Islam**, **Christianity**, **Jainism**, and **Zoroastrianism**.
 
• **Abul Fazl**, the court historian and author of **Akbarnama**, defined the ideal **Mughal** ruler as one who possesses **farr-i-izadi** (divine light) and maintains **Sulh-i-Kul** by ensuring no group undermines the authority of the state or the rights of others.
 
• The policy emphasized an ethical code focused on **justice**, **honesty**, and **kindness**, rather than the strict imposition of any specific religious dogma or **Islamic law**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abolition of Religious Taxes**: To practicalize **Sulh-i-Kul**, **Akbar** abolished the **Jizya** (a tax on non-Muslim subjects) in **1564** and the **Pilgrim Tax** in **1563**, which were previously major sources of resentment among **Hindus**.
 
• **Administrative Integration**:
 
 
• The policy allowed for the large-scale integration of **Rajput** chiefs and other non-Muslims into the high-ranking **Mansabdari** system of the **Mughal** bureaucracy.
 
• It shifted the loyalty of the nobility from their respective religious groups to the person of the **Mughal Emperor**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Successors**: While **Jahangir** and **Shah Jahan** largely followed the principles of **Sulh-i-Kul**, the policy saw a significant reversal during the reign of **Aurangzeb**, who reintroduced the **Jizya** and adopted more orthodox religious stances.

questions.question: Which financial incentive is specifically extended to developers of Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in India to facilitate infrastructure creation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capital grant from central government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Special Economic Zones (SEZs)** in India are designated duty-free enclaves treated as foreign territories for trade operations, duties, and tariffs, governed by the **SEZ Act, 2005**.
 
• To support the high capital expenditure required for developing world-class infrastructure, the central government offers **capital grants** and financial assistance through targeted infrastructure development schemes to eligible SEZ developers.
 
• These grants are aimed at facilitating the creation of essential common infrastructure, such as roads, water supply systems, power distribution networks, and waste management facilities.
 
• In addition to direct funding support, developers are entitled to duty-free import or domestic procurement of goods and a 10-year **Income Tax exemption** under **Section 80-IAB** of the Income Tax Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tax refund on exports**:

 
 
• This fiscal benefit is specifically structured for **SEZ Units** (the individual business entities operating inside the zone) to boost their export competitiveness under **Section 10AA**, rather than for the master developers of the zone.
 
 
 
• **Subsidy on land acquisition**:
 
 
• Land acquisition is primarily governed by **State Governments**. While state policies may facilitate land allotment, there is no standardized central subsidy provided specifically for purchasing land.
 
 
 
• **Low-interest loans from banks**:
 
 
• Although SEZ infrastructure development is granted **infrastructure status** to enable easier access to external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and long-term credit, banks do not offer mandated low-interest loans as a direct government incentive.

questions.question: The next census of India will be conducted by February 28 ______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2027**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Census of India** is the largest administrative and statistical exercise in the world, traditionally conducted every **ten years** to capture the demographic, social, and economic profile of the nation.
 
• The last successful census was conducted in **2011**; however, the scheduled **2021 Census** was postponed indefinitely due to the outbreak of the **COVID-19 pandemic** and the resulting administrative challenges.
 
• The Government of India has indicated that the fieldwork and enumeration for the next census are now targeted for completion by **February 28, 2027**, effectively skipping the 2021 cycle to maintain a new decadal alignment.
 
• This census is of critical importance because its data will be utilized for the **delimitation of parliamentary constituencies** and is a prerequisite for implementing the **Women’s Reservation Act** (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam).
 
• The process involves two main phases: **House Listing and Housing Census** followed by **Population Enumeration**, ensuring every individual residing in the country is accounted for.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Background**:

 
 
• The first non-synchronous census in India was initiated in **1872** during the tenure of **Lord Mayo**.
 
• The first synchronous and comprehensive census was conducted in **1881** under **Lord Ripon**, and it has been held every ten years since then until the 2021 delay.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Authority**:
 
 
• The census is organized by the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, which operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Transition**:
 
 
• The **2027 Census** is expected to be India’s first **Digital Census**, utilizing a specially developed mobile application for data collection and a **Self-Enumeration** portal for citizens.
 
 
 
• **Legal Provisions**:
 
 
• The exercise is conducted under the **Census Act, 1948**, which provides the legal backing for data collection and guarantees the **confidentiality** of the information provided by the public.

questions.question: Which Harappan site is located in Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manda** is a prominent archaeological site of the **Indus Valley Civilization** (IVC) located in the **Akhnoor** district of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
• Geographically, it is situated on the right bank of the **Chenab River** in the foothills of the **Pir Panjal Range**, marking a significant territorial boundary.
 
• It is widely considered the **northernmost point** of the Harappan civilization within the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The site was excavated in **1976-77** by **Jagat Pati Joshi**, revealing a cultural sequence that spans from the **Pre-Harappan** to the **Post-Harappan** eras.
 
• Significant artifacts recovered from Manda include **Harappan redware**, **copper double-headed pins** (of Central Asian origin), **terracotta cakes**, and **chert blades**.
 
• The settlement provided evidence of the **Mature Harappan** culture overlapping with local traditions, suggesting it served as a key outpost for timber and lapis lazuli trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalibangan**:

 
 
• Located in the **Hanumangarh** district of **Rajasthan** on the banks of the **Ghaggar-Hakra River**.
 
• Notable for being the first site to provide evidence of **ploughed agricultural fields** and the presence of **fire altars**.
 
 
 
• **Banawali**:
 
 
• Situated in the **Fatehabad** district of **Haryana**.
 
• Famous for the discovery of a high-quality **terracotta model of a plough** and significant quantities of **barley**.
 
 
 
• **Lothal**:
 
 
• Located in the **Ahmedabad** district of **Gujarat** near the **Sargwala** village.
 
• It was a major port city featuring the world's earliest known **artificial dockyard** connected to the **Sabarmati River**.
